selected_evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created as shared writable directory with sticky bit (users cannot delete others' files)
selected_evidence.summary: Directory created with mode 1777 root:root; two test users each wrote their own file, and cross-user rm attempts failed with 'Operation not permitted', while same-owner writes succeeded.

selected_evidence.requirement: Cleanup left /srv/drop in final clean state
selected_evidence.summary: Test files removed and test users deleted; /srv/drop shown empty with correct 1777 root:root permissions.

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline for node1 (boot identity + service/data health)
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id f41e1f8a-dd2a-4b61-aa04-d64b0923b603 and uptime, plus confirmed /srv/drop (1777 root:root) resides on the persistent root filesystem /dev/vda1, not tmpfs.
systemctl reboot issued in background via nohup; command returned immediately with PID before the node dropped.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node unreachable then reachable again after restart
selected_evidence.summary: First poll got SSH connection refused (node down/rebooting); second poll succeeded, confirming node1 came back online.

selected_evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id is 1d269819-6cfc-45de-9d09-97f937972bae, different from the pre-restart f41e1f8a-... value, and uptime -s shows a new boot time.

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and sticky-bit behavior
selected_evidence.summary: /srv/drop still shows 1777 root:root after reboot; functional re-test with two fresh users confirmed writes succeed and cross-user deletes are still blocked with 'Operation not permitted', then test artifacts were cleaned up leaving /srv/drop empty.
